info.name: Juicebox Laravel API
info.description:
# Juicebox Laravel API

Import this collection and Juicebox.local.postman_environment.json, then select the local environment. Start Laravel with `php artisan serve`. The default base_url is http://127.0.0.1:8000 (do not include /api or a trailing slash).

Set name, email, and password in the environment. Register once with an unused email, or Login with an existing account. These requests automatically save token and user_id as collection variables. Protected requests inherit the collection Bearer authentication. Create post captures post_id for Get, Update, and Delete.

Folders are ordered for a complete run: registration/login → users → post CRUD → weather → logout. A full run creates an account, issues two tokens, creates/deletes a post, and revokes the final token. For repeated runs use a new email, or skip Register and use Login. Avoid running the collection against production data. Registration queues a welcome email using your configured mailer.

Saved examples are illustrative, not captured personal data. For protected requests, 401 indicates missing/revoked credentials, 403 denies changing another author's post, 404 means missing records, and 422 contains field errors. Auth endpoints share a limit of 10 requests/minute/IP; protected endpoints allow 60/minute/user. 429 responses include Retry-After. Weather failures return 503. List endpoints include Laravel data/links/meta pagination.

Do not export populated tokens or real credentials into Git. The supplied files contain only demonstration values.

request.description: Create an account. Required: name (max 255), unique email (max 255), password (minimum 8 characters), and matching password_confirmation. Email is normalized to lowercase. A welcome email is queued after the transaction commits. Saves token and user_id automatically. For another registration, change email to an unused address. Registration itself authenticates you; Login is optional afterward.

request.description: Get current weather for the configured city (Perth by default). Successful responses are cached for 15 minutes; cache misses fetch Open-Meteo. An hourly queued job refreshes the same cache. No API key or location query parameter is required. Configure WEATHER_LOCATION, WEATHER_LATITUDE, WEATHER_LONGITUDE, and WEATHER_TIMEZONE in Laravel .env to change the city. weather_code is a WMO interpretation code. A provider failure or invalid/outdated response returns 503; the success check then fails rather than treating an unavailable provider as success.
